macro_bullets: Fed delivered a hawkish hold with the chair talking tough on inflation, keeping rate-cut expectations in check.
The AI trade is nearing a 'tipping point' as investors like Steve Eisman turn more conservative and data-center capex worries hammer neocloud names.
A memory-chip boom is driving markets, with forecasts of a shortage through 2030 and SK Hynix posting record profits.
Middle East tensions persist as the prolonged Iran war lifts energy prices, with European gas touching €100 and Hormuz disruption hedging underway.
The 'Magnificent Seven' correlation is breaking down, pushing investors to separate winners from losers within Big Tech.
internals_narrative: Memory led all industries at +7.4% with Oracle (+10.7%) and a slate of chip names (SNDK, DRAM, MU, LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) topping gainers, while utilities, communication services and pharma lagged. Losers were led by BKR (-7.4%) despite an earnings beat, alongside BSX (-5.8%) and NOW (-3.0%) on soft guidance.

ticker_notes.ORCL: Oracle's analyst day eased funding concerns and bolstered its growth outlook, with shares up 12% on the week.
ticker_notes.SNDK: SanDisk rode surging flash-memory prices as AI demand makes NAND roughly five times more expensive.
ticker_notes.DRAM: SK Hynix soared on record profit at the top of the memory cycle, though some expect Samsung to lead HBM in 2027.
ticker_notes.MU: Micron was named a top memory-sector pick as forecasts of a shortage through 2030 fueled the rally.
ticker_notes.LRCX: Lam Research drew investor attention amid questions over whether supply constraints will limit its growth.
ticker_notes.IREN: IREN secured $363 million against its GPUs and AI contracts even as neocloud peers gave up recent gains on capex worries.
ticker_notes.AMAT: Applied Materials rose alongside the broad semiconductor equipment rally.
ticker_notes.BKR: Baker Hughes fell despite a Q3 earnings beat and a raised IET outlook, with Piper Sandler trimming its target to $70.
ticker_notes.BSX: Boston Scientific sank after its Q3 call flagged growth challenges through 2027.
ticker_notes.NOW: ServiceNow plunged roughly 19% on an EPS miss and slower backlog guidance, its worst single-day drop in over 14 years.
ticker_notes.ADP: ADP retreated as Q1 results met but didn't exceed a premium valuation.
ticker_notes.VZ: Verizon slipped on signs of a concerning customer trend.
ticker_notes.NEE: NextEra was highlighted among nuclear power stocks to watch.
ticker_notes.AZO: AutoZone's Q4 results exposed cost creep and debt strain ahead of its next report.
ticker_notes.AIG: AIG heads into Q3 earnings with focus on whether higher premiums offset underwriting pressure.
ticker_notes.APD: Air Products is expected to grow earnings as it appoints two new group presidents ahead of its report.
ticker_notes.AMT: American Tower saw price-target cuts from Citi and JPMorgan despite maintained buy ratings.
ticker_notes.AMD: AMD was weighed against Nvidia as Wall Street debates its longer-term AI positioning.
